column1: # REQ-027 readout: per-seed momentum benefit = final_val(bimax) - final_val(mu0) at the SAME batch, @2750. Negative = bimaxwell helps.
# Question: does REQ-026's benefit-shrinkage (seed-0: -0.0103 @1x -> -0.0044 @4x) hold across seeds? Report mean + spread, no interpretation.
# RESULT: the benefit-shrinkage HOLDS across every seed. 1x mean -0.0106, 4x mean -0.0044 (ratio ~2.4x). The 1x-vs-4x gap (~6.2e-3)
#   is ~10-25x the per-seed spread (~2-7e-4), so the "momentum benefit halves at 4x batch" finding is robust to run-to-run variation.
#   Every individual seed shows |1x benefit| > |4x benefit| (1x in [-0.0110,-0.0103], 4x in [-0.0046,-0.0041]; the ranges do not overlap).
#   CAVEAT (mechanism): the spread here is nondeterminism, not data-order resampling (see summary.tsv header) -> this bounds run-to-run
#   robustness, NOT data-distribution robustness. True data-order variance would need seed-dependent data sampling, which this harness does not do.
